title: Hit-and-run by drunk driver kills two women
byline: Two women have tragically lost their lives after being struck by a car on the Embulgama-Panagoda in Hanwella.

title: Divisional Secretaries to boycott Monday meetings from tomorrow
byline: The Sri Lanka Association of Divisional Secretaries and Assistant Divisional Secretaries said that its members will completely withdraw from participating in any official meetings scheduled on Mondays, effective from tomorrow, June 8. This decision applies to all physical as well as virtual (online) meetings usually conducted on this specific day.

title: Manhunt for suspects after 12 people shot near festival in Ohio
byline: Police say they are searching for suspects after at least 12 people were shot near a festival in Toledo, in the midwestern US state of Ohio.

title: Public views sought for new higher education policy framework
byline: The Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education has launched a public consultation process to gather views and recommendations for the formulation of Sri Lanka’s proposed National Higher Education Policy Framework.

title: Iran World Cup team heads to Mexico as US visa row erupts
byline: Iran’s World Cup squad left Turkey for Mexico on Saturday, taking off under the shadow of a bitter diplomatic row between Tehran and Washington after the US refused to issue visas for some of the team’s support squad.

title: Breaking Down the Israel–Iran Conflict: What We Know So Far - Day 100
byline: This guide answers the most important questions about the Israel Iran war that is unfolding right now. The United States and Israel have launched major military strikes on Iran and Iran has responded with missile attacks across the region. This is one of the most serious escalations in the Middle East in years.

title: Suresh Salley being used as a scapegoat, says wife following CID visit
byline: Speaking to the media for the first time outside the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Manory Salley, the wife of former Major General Suresh Salley, defended her husband, insisting that he is innocent and is being unfairly used as a ’’scapegoat.’’

title: White House AI policy adviser Krishnan to leave position
byline: A top White House artificial intelligence policy adviser ‌on Saturday said he will leave his position at the end of June, marking the exit of a leading figure helping craft policies for frontier technologies.

title: Anthropic urges AI labs to pause development, warns humans risk losing control
byline: Anthropic is calling on major artificial intelligence labs to consider a coordinated and verifiable ​pause in development, warning that rapid advances in the technology could soon allow AI systems to improve themselves faster than society ‌can manage the risks.

title: Reservoirs 63% full, water secured for Yala season: Irrigation Department
byline: The 73 major reservoirs managed by the Irrigation Department have collectively reached 63 percent of their total storage capacity, providing sufficient water to meet irrigation requirements for the ongoing Yala cultivation season, officials said.

title: Fishermen, naval community warned to stay ashore as seas turn dangerous
byline: The Natural Hazards Early Warning Centre has issued a Red Warning for strong winds and rough seas, effective from 6.30 a.m. on June 7 until 10.30 a.m. today (8), urging fishing and naval communities to take immediate precautions.

title: SJB expels five Bulathsinhala Pradeshiya Sabha members over bribery allegations
byline: The Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) has decided to strip five of its members representing the Bulathsinhala Pradeshiya Sabha of their positions. The expelled members include SJB Group Leader Nihal Mendis, Mohamed Nishard, Kanthi Pelawatta, Ayesha Chamali, and Pushpa Samarasinghe.

title: US eyes Iranian assets for Gulf allies’ reconstruction, source says
byline: The U.S. government will attempt to redirect ​Iranian assets to Gulf states for rebuilding and repairs of damage caused by Iran, a source familiar with the matter said, as Tehran followed up a wave of strikes ‌against Kuwait and Bahrain with further drone launches.

title: South Korea nominates Han Seong-sook as country’s first female prime minister in two decades
byline: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has ⁠chosen Han Seong-sook, the country’s ⁠minister for small and midsize ‌businesses and ​startups, to be prime minister, the presidential office said on Sunday.

title: Western Province DS offices recognised for President’s fund drive
byline: Divisional Secretariat offices that recorded the highest level of performance under the President’s Fund decentralisation programme in 2025 were honoured at a special recognition ceremony held yesterday (06) at the Miloda Auditorium in Colombo.

title: Huge crowds throng Madrid streets for Pope’s open-air mass
byline: More than a million people lined the streets of Madrid on Sunday as Pope Leo XIV held an open-air mass in the Spanish capital, the Vatican said.

title: Major food supplier fined for selling expired products
byline: A leading food supplier in Nugegoda has been fined Rs. 75,000 and ordered to destroy a stock of food items after pleading guilty to multiple consumer protection violations.

title: Private buses to slash services by 50% over fare dispute
byline: Commuters across Sri Lanka could face major transport disruptions from tomorrow as private bus operators have decided to cut services by 50 percent, citing mounting losses, rising fuel costs, and the government’s failure to grant fare relief.

title: CAASL chief named Asia-Pacific Aviation Security chair
byline: Sri Lanka has secured a key leadership role in regional aviation security, with the Director General and Chief Executive Officer of Civil Aviation, Captain Daminda Rambukwella, being appointed Chairman of the Asia-Pacific Aviation Security Programme (CASP-AP) for 2026/2027.

title: Suresh Sallay’s treatment under PTA is deeply troubling - Namal Rajapaksa
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer Namal Rajapaksa said that concerns raised before court by the legal counsel of Major General (Retd.) Suresh Sallay regarding his treatment in custody, was deeply troubling and asked why activists who were against the PTA maintained such a silence.

title: Wife arrested over stabbing of husband in Horana
byline: A woman has been arrested in connection with the fatal stabbing of her husband following a domestic dispute in the Arambakanda area of the Horana Police Division during the early hours of Sunday (June 7).

title: Heavy rain, strong winds forecast across several areas
byline: The Department of Meteorology has forecast continued showers and thunderstorms across several parts of the country, with heavy rainfall and strong winds expected in some areas.

title: South Korea nominates Han Seong-sook as country’s first female prime minister in two decades
byline: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has ⁠chosen Han Seong-sook, the country’s ⁠minister for small and midsize ‌businesses and ​startups, to be prime minister, the presidential office said on Sunday.

title: Huge crowds throng Madrid streets for Pope’s open-air mass
byline: More than a million people lined the streets of Madrid on Sunday as Pope Leo XIV held an open-air mass in the Spanish capital, the Vatican said.

title: Suresh Sallay admitted to National Hospital
byline: Former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Director, Suresh Sallay, has been admitted to the Emergency Treatment Unit (ETU) of the National Hospital of Sri Lanka.

title: Govt. to revive 25 stalled health projects at cost of Rs. 76Bn
byline: The Government has commenced a programme to revive and complete 25 major health infrastructure projects that were abandoned midway, with an estimated investment of Rs. 76 billion needed to finish the developments.
